fact: ITWeb Africa reports that Lesotho's MICSTI is introducing the Electronic Transactions and Communications Bill, 2026, a revision of the 2022 bill of the same name, after a two-day stakeholder validation workshop held with UNDP that week; the draft goes next to the Office of the Parliamentary Counsel for refinement (as_of is the article's published date, 2026-09-30, the workshop being 'this week').

The ministry states, per ITWeb Africa, that Lesotho lacks a legal and regulatory framework for electronic transactions, creating uncertainty for government, businesses and consumers over electronic contracts, signatures, records, online services and digital commerce (as_of is the article's published date, 2026-09-30).

The Government of Lesotho (via LENA) reports that MICSTI opened a two-day validation workshop in Maseru from Monday (2026-09-28) on the Electronic Transactions and Communications Bill, 2026, to gather stakeholder views before the Bill progresses through the next legislative stages; the Bill is under UNDP supervision and sponsored by MICSTI.

MICSTI's ICT Director states that the absence of a legal and regulatory framework on electronic transactions has created uncertainty for government, businesses and consumers, particularly for electronic contracts, signatures, records, online services and digital commerce.

FinMark Trust says that Lesotho, with the DRC and Zimbabwe, does not have comprehensive legislation on electronic transactions, though many SADC countries have an Electronic Transactions Act; no date is given for the statement, so as_of is the blog's published date, 2026-06-18.
